title: In Mexico, Collectives Will March This Sunday in Defense of Cuba and Anti-Imperialism
author: Iván Evair Saldaña and Jessica Xantomila
content:
_This article by Iván Evair Saldaña and Jessica Xantomila originally appeared
in the[July 24, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/24/politica/colectivos-
marcharan-este-domingo-en-defensa-de-cuba-y-el-antimperialismo), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

Social organizations expect this Sunday's march in defense of Cuba in Mexico
City to be massive, with a turnout larger than that of the mobilizations held
every July 26 for decades, to protest mainly the hardening of Donald Trump's
government policy against the island and Washington's measures directed at
other countries and progressive movements.

Olivia Garza Joa, vice president of the José Martí Association of Cubans
Residing in Mexico, explained that for more than a month, Cuba solidarity
organizations, social movements, urban and popular collectives, unions,
parties, and other groups met to organize a united march.

> "We ask that they join in the defense of Cuba in the face of the imminent
> danger of a military invasion. Also, for the sovereignty, independence, and
> self-determination of all of our America," she told La Jornada.

The march, which commemorates the 73rd anniversary of the assaults on the
Moncada and Carlos Manuel de Céspedes barracks, led by Fidel Castro in 1953,
also seeks to raise awareness about the actions of U.S. Secretary of State
Marco Rubio, who aims to "counteract every progressive or social movement."

> She added: "We think we have to stay alert and start mobilizing people."

She detailed that the march will have an anti-imperialist character and will
express rejection of measures such as the tariffs imposed on Brazil and "the
fraud of the elections in Peru and Colombia," as well as other Washington
actions in Latin America.

## They Will Depart from the Hemiciclo

The mobilization will depart at 10:30 a.m. from the Hemiciclo a Juárez heading
to the former United States embassy. At the end, a single statement, agreed
upon by the participating organizations to express a common position, will be
read.

The event will include the participation of some artists, although the main
objective will be to establish a political position in defense of Cuba and of
Latin America's sovereignty, she stressed.

> "We managed to put support for Cuba above the ideological differences that
> sometimes exist with some organizations," she noted.

In addition to the march, various political and cultural commemorative events,
such as exhibitions and discussion panels, are also being held in Mexico City
and other states.

This anniversary has particular importance at a time when the United States
blockade against the island has intensified.
